market_context.summary: Sunday run; US equities and futures are shut, so every equity level below is for the Monday 2026-08-24 open and every equity price is the Friday 2026-08-21 close. The tape is priced for a hawkish Fed, not an easing one: Kalshi puts a 31-32% probability on a 25bp HIKE at the September 16 FOMC and essentially zero on any cut in 2026, fed funds futures imply nearer 40%, and the effective funds rate sits at 3.63% against a 4.69% 10-year. The 30-year yield at 5.23% is at multi-decade highs and the curve is steepening from the long end (30y-10y +54bp, 10y-2y +50bp), which is a term-premium and fiscal story rather than a growth one - consistent with US debt passing $40 trillion, an unexpected Treasury announcement doubling long-bond buybacks, gold up 14% in three weeks and the dollar reportedly breaking below 99. Against all that, VIX closed at 16.01. The market is priced for calm going into a week that stacks July PCE and the Q2 GDP second estimate (Wed 08:30 ET), NVIDIA earnings (Wed after the close) and Chair Warsh's first Jackson Hole keynote (Fri ~10:00 ET). Cheap volatility ahead of concentrated event risk is why the ideas below are sized small and why seven of eleven say wait rather than buy.

catalyst.event: The July 14 2026 pre-announcement is the setup, not a coming event: IBM fell ~25% in one session, its worst day on record and worse than October 19 1987, erasing about $69B - on adjusted EPS of $2.93 against $3.01 expected and revenue of $17.2B against $17.86B. The driver from here is whether the deals that slipped out of Q2 close in Q3 and Q4. The next Q3 report in October is the first real test.
catalyst.action: DO NOT BUY AT 235.68 - the reward-to-risk there is 1.19 and does not clear the long-term floor. Leave a limit at 215 with a 206-224 zone and accept that it may never fill. This is a wait recommendation with a price attached, not an order to place today.

recommendations.thesis: IBM lost about $69B of market value in a single session on a 2.7% EPS miss and a 3.7% revenue miss - the worst day in its history, worse than October 1987 - and CEO Arvind Krishna gave a specific, checkable reason: in the final weeks of June, clients redirected budget from IBM software and infrastructure toward servers, storage and memory chips to lock in supply-constrained hardware ahead of price increases, and large deals slipped past their expected close dates. Budget that moves forward a quarter to beat a price increase is deferred revenue, not lost revenue. The stock has since held a tight 228.85-238.42 range for three weeks, so the forced selling is finished and what remains is a question about whether those deals close.
recommendations.key_risk: The invalidation is precise and dated to the reports rather than the price: if Q3 and Q4 software revenue does not recover the deals that slipped out of Q2, then the shift was share loss dressed up as timing and IBM breaks its 199.19 post-crash low. The market clearly leans that way - a 25% reaction to a 3.7% miss is a verdict on forward execution, not on one quarter - and the CEO has publicly conceded the company fell behind. Note also there is no insider support here: the only two open-market buys totalled $113K and predate the crash.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against is simply the size of the reaction. Markets do not erase $69B over a rounding error unless they have decided the growth story is broken, and a CEO who did not see a spending shift coming three weeks before quarter-end is telling you something about the visibility of the pipeline. If enterprise budget is structurally migrating from IBM software to hardware in an AI buildout, no amount of deal-timing arithmetic saves the multiple.

What is NOT new is the rate regime: those are the highest levels since late June, so the market has already had two months to price half-a-million-dollar days.
catalyst.action: Hold. Raise the stop from 17.60 to 18.30. TARGET RESTORED TO 22.50 by the red team — the synthesis phase raised it to 24.50 and that number is not defensible (see thesis). Add inside 18.80-20.10 only if not already at full size. Cut the whole position on a credible Hormuz de-escalation headline regardless of price.

recommendations.thesis: Update to the 2026-08-18 long: hold with the stop raised to 18.30 and the target left at 22.50. DHT is a pure-play VLCC owner and VLCC spot earnings on the Middle East Gulf to China route are above $520,000 a day against a normal baseline of $20,000-$60,000, because ships are routing around the Strait of Hormuz and adding ton-miles. Rates at this level convert almost entirely to cash for an owner whose fleet is already on the water. RED TEAM CHANGE: synthesis raised the target from 22.50 to 24.50 at the same time it raised the stop from 17.60 to 18.30, and both moves push the ratio up — together they took the published reward-to-risk from 1.72 to 4.64 on a four-day-old position. Raising a stop on a winner is sound; the target raise is not. DHT's entire 120-day range is 15.98-20.62, so 24.50 sits 18.8% above the highest price the stock has traded in four months with no NAV, earnings or cash-flow anchor offered, and validation independently flagged it at 7.07 ATR against a 6.0 guide. The freight rates are not new either — they are the highest since late June, and the market has already seen them and answered with a 20.62 high. The 22.50 target is itself still 9% above that high, so this is not a conservative number. Conviction cut 4 to 3: a single geopolitical spot rate that the report itself says will gap through the stop is not where the size should be.
recommendations.key_risk: The entire thesis is one geopolitical spot rate. A credible Hormuz de-escalation would take VLCC earnings from $520,000 back toward $60,000 in days, and the stock would gap through the 18.30 stop rather than trade to it. This is why the stop is a discipline rather than a guarantee, and why the position is sized at 2% and not more.
recommendations.counter_argument: Rates this far above baseline are by definition unsustainable, and the market knows it - which is exactly why DHT trades at 19.82 rather than at a multiple of it. Paying up for a spot spike that everyone can see, after the stock has already recovered to within 4% of its high, is late by construction.

catalyst.event: FDA PDUFA action date for MOLBREEVI (molgramostim inhalation solution) in autoimmune pulmonary alveolar proteinosis, extended from Aug 22 to November 22 2026. catalyst.action: Accumulate in the 5.15-5.60 zone over the next few weeks while the delay is still the story. Do not add above 6.00. Hold into the November decision.

recommendations.thesis: Savara is a $1.15B company (205,460,015 shares per the Q2 10-Q cover, at the 5.59 close) whose only asset, MOLBREEVI, is a first-in-class inhaled GM-CSF for autoimmune pulmonary alveolar proteinosis - a disease with no approved therapy - backed by a positive Phase 3 (IMPALA-2). The August 22 PDUFA was pushed to November 22 on a major-amendment technicality, with the FDA explicitly not raising safety, efficacy or manufacturing concerns, and the stock sits 13.7% below its 120-day high on that administrative delay. Capital position was $202.8M against roughly $33M of quarterly operating burn, so the runway reaches into mid-2027, past the new decision date. Average dollar volume is about $8M a day and was $17M on Friday, far above the liquidity floor.
recommendations.key_risk: This is a conviction-2 idea and the evidence is one-sided by construction: a single-asset biotech where a Complete Response Letter in November is a 50%+ down day with no second product to fall back on. Savara has also filed a $108.3M shelf covering up to 18.9M shares - 9.2% of the 205.5M shares outstanding - so a capital raise into or after the decision is a quantified dilution risk on top of the binary. Size it as a lottery ticket, not a position, and expect 5% daily moves given the 4.8% ATR.
recommendations.counter_argument: A major amendment is exactly what the FDA calls it when a sponsor has had to substantially rewrite part of a submission, and the agency not citing safety or efficacy in a press release is not the same as the reviewers being satisfied. Three extra months of review on a single-asset company also brings the raise three months closer.

recommendations.counter_argument: A dollar falling because investors are worried about US fiscal solvency is not the same as a dollar falling because global growth is improving, and only the second kind is reliably good for emerging markets. If the long end keeps selling off, EM dollar-debt costs rise even as the dollar falls, and EEM can decline with a weak dollar rather than because of it. Yesterday's report made this point against itself and then dissolved it by flipping the house Fed view overnight: it wrote that you cannot hold a hawkish-Fed house view and a conviction-3 short-dollar equity trade at the same time, and cut EEM to conviction 2 for exactly that reason. The contradiction was resolved by changing the Fed view, not by resolving the evidence. Conviction 2 is the honest carry.

RESEARCH COMPLETE — the research phase finished inside its budget and then went back to close a macro gap and add one more idea, so nothing here is a truncation artefact. All eleven candidates are published; nothing cleared the bar and was cut for space or variety.

PRICES. This is a Sunday run with US equities and futures shut. Every equity and ETF price is the Friday 2026-08-21 close (finnhub or nasdaq, session=closed, ~39 hours old). SOURCES THAT FAILED. Yahoo Finance returned HTTP 429 on every symbol, stooq 404s on all index tickers, and finnhub refuses index CFDs, so market_data.py's macro block produced no fetched quote for SPX, NDX, DJI, RUT, VIX, DXY, gold, WTI, ES or NQ. FRED was used afterwards to recover the 30-year (5.23%), VIX (16.01), WTI ($86.48) and the broad dollar index — those figures are primary-sourced. Two figures in the market summary are NOT: the 'dollar below 99.00' and the gold spot level come from news text, not a price feed. The Fed's broad trade-weighted index (118.90) is not on the same scale as DXY and neither confirms nor contradicts it. WebFetch got 403 from cnbc.com and from sec.gov/Archives, so the CNBC week-ahead is quoted from its search summary and no filing was read in full HTML.

UNVERIFIED FIELDS. market_cap_usd is an order-of-magnitude estimate on every equity except SVRA — no share count was fetched for CCJ, PFE, NKE, LULU, VST, DHT or IBM. REWARD-TO-RISK. Every ratio was recomputed during synthesis from the final entry, target and downside in the file — the stop for swing ideas, the stated bear-case price for long-term — and all eleven match what research reported. Be aware of a genuine cluster just above the floors: LULU 2.65, VST 2.65, TLT 2.68 and NKE 2.69 all sit within 0.2 of their bar, and the Fed contract is at exactly 2.00.
